unit.why: A minimal anecdote: at a festive meal a guest says he is not a hasid, the rebbe objects, and the rest is a long homily on why the name 'tsaddik' gave way to 'hasid'. The homily takes up most of the text.

stories.start_quote: עוד שם ששמע מפיו הקדוש פ"א
stories.summary_en: At a festive meal one guest shrugs that he is 'not a hasid'. The rebbe is displeased and explains, through Isaiah's verse, that Satan replaced the old pair tsaddik/rasha with 'hasid' so that sinners need not be ashamed, so no one should exclude himself from the hasidim.

tags.why: The short incident is wrapped in an extended exegetical homily.

quotes: וזאת יספר לנו ישעי׳ הנביא בפסוק הצדיק אבד
והקפיד ע״ז הרה״ק ואמר כי ח"ו
tags.why: The rebbe is displeased by the remark.
The exchange is about a Jew who declares he is not a hasid.

quotes: אם במלבושי רשע או בבית התפלה
tags.why: Jewish versus wicked dress is a marker of righteousness in the homily.

quotes: שלא יתבייש לעשות מה שלבו חפץ
tags.why: The homily turns on social shame as what kept the wicked in check.

quotes: הולך בחקות העכו"ם שעטנז מגדל בלורית

tags.why: In the old order, shame forced the wicked to repent.

quotes: אם בבית התפלה להתפלל באימה וביראה
tags.why: The house of prayer is mentioned as a place of conduct.

missing_concepts: the term 'hasid' versus 'tsaddik' as identity labels
Satan (ba'al davar) as a scheming concept, not a character
